newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai parliament starts process to name new premier.
newsitem.headline: Thai parliament starts process to name new premier.

text.p: Thailand's parliament reconvenes on Saturday to start the process of appointing New Aspiration Party (NAP) leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh the country's 22nd prime minister.

The NAP won a narrow two-seat victory over the Democrat Party in a general election on November 17. It has formed a six-party coalition which will have a comfortable majority of 221 seats in the 393-seat parliament.
The party ousted the 14-month old trouble-plagued coalition of Chart Thai leader Banharn Silpa-archa.
Thailand's King Bhumibol Adulyadej will open the house session on Saturday in a royal ceremony at 1030 GMT.

The first sitting of the house will begin about 90 minutes later to elect a president of the parliament -- the person who will propose the name of the leader of the dominant party as prime minister to the king for royal approval.
The NAP is expected to nominate deputy party leader Wan Muhamad Nor Matha as the parliament president so he can ensure Chavalit's name is submitted for the premiership.
The Democrat-led opposition will nominate former leader Bhichai Rattakul for the post, but he is not expected to win since the NAP-led coalition has the majority in parliament.

Analysts and politicians say this is expected to take place by Monday, in time for Chavalit to be the new leader so he can welcome U.S. president Bill Clinton who arrives in Bangkok late on Monday for a brief state visit to Thailand.
Chavalit has been embroiled in intense negotiations with his coalition partners over the makeup of the cabinet since his election victory last Sunday.

The main delay has stemmed from differences over how to share out economic portfolios, coalition sources said. The coalition has given the economy top priority and vowed to appoint a qualified economic team to improve a slowing economy.
Chavalit said on Thursday he expects to complete the cabinet next week.
